predecessors.name: Shunten and Eiso dynasties (Okinawa)
predecessors.text: central Okinawa around Urasoe: 'Okinawa split into these three more solidly defined kingdoms within a few years after 1314; the Sanzan period thus began'

successors.name: Ryukyu Kingdom
successors.text: the united island of Okinawa: infobox 'Succeeded by: Ryukyu Kingdom', 'Ryukyuan unification: 1429'

ledger.x: 1314: Chūzan arises at Urasoe as one of the three kingdoms of Okinawa.
1350: the Satto line takes the Chūzan throne from the Eiso line.
1372: the first Ming envoys reach Okinawa and Chūzan becomes a tributary of Ming China.
1407: the First Shō dynasty begins with Shō Shishō.
1416: Shō Hashi attacks Hokuzan at Nakijin.
1416: the fighting ends with the fall of Nakijin Castle ('Following a fierce defense, Nakijin castle fell').
1429: Shō Hashi moves against Nanzan after Taromai's death.
1429: Chūzan takes Nanzan and Okinawa is one.
1429: the conquest of Nanzan is complete ('marking the end of the independent kingdom of Nanzan').

1429: Chūzan ceases as a Ming tributary because it ceases to exist; the relation passes to the Ryukyu Kingdom, whose infobox status reads 'Tributary state of the Ming dynasty (1429–1644)' (recorded in ryukyu-kingdom).
1429: the three kingdoms are united as the Ryukyu Kingdom.

wars.name: Chūzan's conquest of Hokuzan
wars.outcome: Chūzan victory: Nakijin Castle fell after three anji defected and the Hokuzan king and his closest vassals killed themselves.

wars.name: Chūzan's conquest of Nanzan
wars.outcome: Chūzan victory: Shō Hashi took Nanzan after Taromai's death and united the island as the Ryukyu Kingdom.

certainty.note: A castle-lord realm of districts with no recorded frontier; the borders with Hokuzan and Nanzan are approximate.
